title: One live archetype-registry reader: grid cache and fairness gate follow edits
shared_surfaces: perf-budget.json (only if test:perf shows the task-hub or app/page.tsx graph grew; archetype-live.ts is server-only and lands on the screen-wave/automation-pass graph, not the client shell)

app/_lib/automation-fairness.ts:23/:50 re-asserts Python's reject with the same bundled gate, while pipeline/jobfit/automation.py:313 derives _EARLY_CAREER from the live file — the two runtimes read two copies, which the governing technique names as the failure mode
rollback: Three commits (reader + tests; matrix key axis; gate call sites + docs) revert cleanly: the bundled exports in archetypes.ts keep their signatures and client importers are untouched, the matrix LRU is in-memory (a revert just changes keys, no persisted state), and the live gate is a union with the bundled one, so reverting can only return to the pre-change shield, never a weaker one.
runner_up: Fold the registry digest into the analyze cache key (cache-key.ts) so a detection/weights edit stops serving stale v2Profile routing — deferred because the digest must be threaded through analyze-run.ts, which two r07 cards rewrite.
body:
## Summary
The archetype taxonomy has one editable file but two physical reads: Python re-reads pipeline/jobfit/archetypes.json on every spawn, while the TS fairness gate and the matrix grid cache answer from a copy frozen at build time. Add one server-only live reader (mtime/size-memoised, content-digested, validated, fail-closed) and make the two server consumers that decide or cache on the registry follow it.

## Description
Today an operator can change the registry at runtime (create a custom archetype, flip a custom archetype's fairness flag, reweight a built-in). Python honours the change on its next spawn. The TS side does not: (1) GET /api/matrix keeps serving the pre-edit grid, because its content-addressed key hashes profiles and jobs but not the weights the scorer used, and the LRU has no TTL; (2) screen-wave and the automation re-check shield or refuse on the bundled copy, so a custom archetype registered after build is audited as 'Unknown archetype' on every wave, and a custom archetype whose shield is switched ON at runtime is still auto-reject-eligible in TS until the next deploy. The move: `app/_lib/archetype-live.ts` exposes `archetypeRegistryDigest()`, `liveIsKnownArchetype()` and `isFairnessProtectedLive()` (shield = bundled OR live OR unknown — it can only ever add protection), invalidated by `writeRegistry`. The digest becomes an explicit axis of `matrixCacheKey`. archetypes.ts keeps its client-safe exports; the pure gate predicate is factored so both readers share one rule.

## Flow
1. Write archetype-live.test.ts cases 1-5 and the matrix-cache digest case against a temp registry path (reader takes an injectable path).
2. Implement archetype-live.ts: statSync mtime+size memo, sha1 digest of bytes, validate through the same validator archetype-registry uses, fall back to the bundle on any failure.
3. archetype-registry.ts writeRegistry calls invalidateLiveRegistry() after rename.
4. matrix-cache.ts adds `registryDigest`; api/matrix/route.ts passes archetypeRegistryDigest().
5. screen-wave.ts and automation-fairness.ts swap to the live gate; the unknown-archetype audit fires only when the id is unknown to BOTH readers.
6. Update docs/features/candidates/README.md (registry section) and docs/features/pipeline/README.md (fairness gate) — append-only, both docs are also touched by r07 cards.

## Expected impact
A registry edit takes effect on the TS side in the same process that accepted it: the grid re-scores after a reweight instead of lying until an LRU eviction, the fairness shield can be switched on for a custom population without a redeploy, and the audit trail stops calling a registered archetype 'Unknown'. The one-read invariant the header comment claims becomes true for every server decision.

## Evaluation
Claim: every server-side registry consumer that decides or caches follows the live file, and the shield can only grow.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate — node:test (archetype-live.test.ts, matrix-cache.test.ts, automation-fairness.test.ts, a screen-wave unit-db case) inside npm run test:unit, plus tsc, lint, test:perf.
Result: pending build.
Gate: policy-tighten

title: Before Apply, show who on today's board the floor move pulls into reach

The catalog keys are append-only in one commit under the shared-surface lock, so reverting that commit plus the feature commits returns the tree exactly; nothing persists (the preview is a dry run).

body:
## Summary
The calibration panel asks an operator to move the live auto-reject floor on historical evidence, but never shows what the move does to the candidates on the board today. The app already has the exact predicate (screen-wave's dry run). Put a named preview beside the Apply button: per role, who enters auto-reject reach, who leaves it, and who is fairness-shielded from it.

## Description
Today Apply is a blind policy change: the card states a band's past advance rate and the floor numbers, the click writes the floor, and the confirmation repeats the numbers. The next screening wave then previews a reject set the operator never connected to that click. The leap is to show consequence at the moment of decision. `calibration-recommendation.ts` extracts the live-recommendation derivation so apply and preview can never diverge. `floor-move-preview.ts` enumerates the workspace's roles with active Screened entries and runs `runScreenWave(jobId, override, {dryRun:true}, ws)` under the current rule and under the rule with the suggested floor (global or familyFloors[family]); a pure `diffFloorMove` turns the two decision lists into entering / leaving / shielded rows. `GET /api/analytics/calibration/floor-preview` (operator + pipeline:write, rate-limited like apply-threshold, not admitted by public-routes.ts) serves it; `floorPreviewView.ts` shapes it and ThresholdSuggestion renders it under the sentence, with names deep-linking to the board. It reuses existing refusal codes, so no new error codes are added; new catalog keys are the copy only.

## Flow
1. Write floor-move-preview.test.ts (unit-db) and floorPreviewView.test.ts cases first.
2. Extract calibration-recommendation.ts from apply-threshold/route.ts:79-95; point apply-threshold at it (behaviour unchanged, its tests stay green).
3. Implement floor-move-preview.ts (dry-run pair per role + pure diff).
4. Add the floor-preview route with requireOperator, can('pipeline:write'), rateLimit; add the rate-limit contract row; run npm run api:docs.
5. floorPreviewView.ts + ThresholdSuggestion block (tokens and recipes only, both themes); catalog keys in all four locales in one commit.
6. Update docs/features/analytics/README.md (calibration section; append-only, an r07 card also touches this doc).

## Expected impact
Moving the floor stops being a number-only decision: the operator sees '3 candidates on Backend Engineer would come into auto-reject reach: Novák 42, ... ; 1 shielded (early-career)' before clicking, and can decline a move whose live effect is wrong. It also closes the recommend -> apply -> surprise gap the next screening wave used to open.

## Evaluation
Claim: before Apply, the panel names who on today's board the suggested floor moves, per role, using the same predicate the wave will use, and writes nothing.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate — node:test (floor-move-preview.test.ts on unit-db, floorPreviewView.test.ts, route.test.ts, rate-limit-contract.test.ts) in npm run test:unit, plus i18n:check, api:check, design:check, test:perf.
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract
